blockNote: COP commands for script flow, event flags, scene changes, randomness and music loading. Commands (id, uses in extracted/ at I025): 00 Yield (0), 03 LoopStart (229), 04 LoopNext (228), 05 WaitWhileFlagEquals (70), 06 Jump (0), 07 JumpIfFlagEquals (190), 08 JumpIfFlagNotEquals (7), 09 SetOrClearFlag (213), 10 SetNextScene (65), 14 JumpIfSwitchSet (245), 1B DelayThenGoto (211), 1F StepRandom (49), 27 YieldThenGoto (81), 31 FadeAndLoadMusic (9), 32 StopAndLoadMusic (5), 35 RandomMod (9), 3B JumpIfSwitchSetElseHold (28), 3C SetTransitionType (23), 91 SetEntryHere (414). Conventions shared by all handlers: cop_core block note.
=== RESUME POINTER AND WAITS ===

An actor script runs when its wait counter $14 goes below 0 (the actor loop in engine_scheduler_sprites_combat_collision decrements it every frame). A yield (CopExitYield, or a plain RTL in the script) returns to the actor loop; the next run starts at the resume address $18,X in the bank $36,X. So a command that must repeat sets or keeps $18,X: Cop91 stores the address after itself (a script that is COP 91 ... RTL re-runs from there every frame), Cop1B stores a target plus a delay in $14 (the script runs delay + 1 frames later), Cop27 stores a target and clears $14 (next frame), Cop03/Cop04 keep a loop start in $2C and a counter in $2E (one loop per actor, no nesting; $2E is also the monsters-left counter of the lair scripts). Cop05 rewinds $38 to the COP instruction itself so the wait re-tests every frame. Two commands in a row, COP 03 (#N) and COP 04 with nothing between, are a pause of N frames.
=== FLAG WORDS AND SWITCHES ===

Event flags (cop_core.TestEventFlag, WriteEventFlag): a word with the bit number in bits 0-7, the byte index into event_flags ($1A5E) in bits 8-14 and a sense bit v in bit 15. Cop05 waits while the flag equals v, Cop07 jumps when it equals v, Cop08 when it differs from v, Cop09 writes v. Switches are a second bit array at $1ADE addressed by the lair record index (data_00BA0D, 32 bytes per record): Cop14 and Cop3B test them and register the calling actor in switch_owner_table; HoldActorUntilReleased (engine_003005) sets the bits.
=== SCENES, RANDOM, MUSIC ===

Cop10 writes scene_next ($0318; the main loop's loader starts when it is non-zero) and the arrival point warp_dest_*; Cop3C chooses the transition style first. Cop1F and Cop35 are the random pair (state $0302-$0311 of rng_state). Cop31 and Cop32 spawn the music-load actor (MusicLoadSendFade / MusicLoadSendStop in engine_spawn_lairs_death_drops, section MUSIC LOAD AND RESPAWN): the operand is a track number, an index into table_00FB49 (21 long pointers); the numbers used are $00, $02, $0D, $11, $12 and $13.

Cop00_Yield: Yields without touching the resume pointer.
When: no script uses it (0 uses; OQ-I025-4).
Why: spare entry of the command table; the same effect is an RTL in the script.
Out: leaves through CopExitYield; the actor loop runs the script again at the unchanged resume address $18,X.
Cop03_LoopStart: Starts a counted loop of the script.
When: 229 scripts, always paired with Cop04.
Sees: a repeated action; with nothing between Cop03 and Cop04 it is a pause of about N frames (#$3D = 61 frames).
Why: the script language has no other loop; the loop state lives in the actor itself, so an actor has one loop at a time (no nesting) and $2C/$2E are not free for the lair scripts' own counters.
In: Byte = number of passes N; X = actor.
Out: $2E,X = N, $2C,X and $18,X = address of the first command after this one; continues there (leaves through CopExitJump with A = $38).
Cop04_LoopNext: Ends one pass of the loop started by Cop03.
When: 228 scripts, after the body of a Cop03 loop.
Sees: the body repeats; when the body yields (wait, animation) each pass lasts that long.
In: no operand; X = actor with $2C = loop start and $2E = counter.
Out: $2E,X decremented; zero: continues after this command; non-zero: $18,X = $2C,X (the loop start) and yield, so the body runs again next frame.
Cop05_WaitWhileFlagEquals: Waits while an event flag has the value v given in bit 15 of the flag word.
Sees: a scripted actor stands still until a story flag changes (set elsewhere by Cop09).
Why: event flags are the only state shared between actors, and this is the blocking wait on them.
In: Word = flag word (bits 0-7 bit number, bits 8-14 byte index into $1A5E, bit 15 = v).

Out: flag == v: dp$38 is rewound by 2 (id and opcode bytes) to the COP instruction itself, saved as the resume pointer, and the actor yields (it re-tests next frame); flag != v: skips the word and continues.
Cop06_Jump: When: no script uses it (0 uses; OQ-I025-4).
Why: complete command set (a plain BRA/BRL in the script does the same).
Out: the script continues at the target (CopExitJump).
Cop07_JumpIfFlagEquals: Jumps when an event flag has the value v given in bit 15 of the flag word.
When: 190 scripts, the commonest flag branch.
Sees: NPC dialogue and behaviour depend on story progress (before/after a released NPC or an opened door).
Why: one command for both polarities: v = 1 jumps when the flag is set, v = 0 when it is clear.
In: Word = flag word (bit 15 = v), &Code = target.
Out: flag == v: jump; otherwise skips the four operand bytes (CopExitSkip4). The test is in CopFlagJumpTail.
Cop08_JumpIfFlagNotEquals: Jumps when an event flag differs from the value v given in bit 15 of the flag word.
Sees: same as Cop07, with the opposite branch.
Why: Cop07 with the sense bit inverted (EOR #$8000) before the shared test.
In: Word = flag word (bit 15 = v), &Code = target.
Out: flag != v: jump; otherwise CopExitSkip4.
CopFlagJumpTail: Shared tail of Cop07 and Cop08: tests the flag word in A and jumps or skips the operands.
When: Cop07 branches here, Cop08 falls in after inverting bit 15.
In: A = flag word, dp$38 at the flag word; bit 15 set = jump when the flag is set, clear = jump when it is clear.
Out: jump: dp$38 moves past the flag word, the &Code word is read and the script continues there (CopExitJump); no jump: CopExitSkip4.
Cop09_SetOrClearFlag: Sets or clears an event flag.
Sees: story progress is recorded (an NPC was talked to, a switch was pulled); Cop05, Cop07 and Cop08 in other scripts see it later.
Why: all progress flags are in one bit array, written by this one command.
In: Word = flag word: bit 15 set = set the flag, clear = clear it; bits 0-14 select the flag.
Cop10_SetNextScene: Requests a scene change and sets the arrival point.
When: 65 scripts (doors, stairs and the end of cutscenes; ends in RTL).
Sees: the screen changes (style from Cop3C) and the next scene loads with the player at the given position and animation.
Why: a scene change is just a value in scene_next; the main loop starts the loader when it is non-zero.
In: Word = area in the low byte and scene in the high byte (#$0104 = area $04, scene $01); Byte = arrival animation; Word = arrival x; Word = arrival y.

Out: scene_next ($0318) = scene low byte, area high byte (XBA); warp_dest_anim ($0380), warp_dest_x ($037C), warp_dest_y ($037E) = the three arrival values (SpawnPlacementList puts the player at x and y + 16).
Cop14_JumpIfSwitchSet: Registers the actor as the owner of a switch and jumps when the switch is already set.
When: 245 scripts, the first command of nearly every placed NPC or object: COP 14 (#switch, &Active) followed by RTL, so the actor polls its switch every frame.
Sees: the NPC, chest or door becomes active (appears) once its lair is cleared or its switch is triggered; before that nothing.
Why: bit n of the array at $1ADE is switch n, the lair record index of data_00BA0D; the actor keeps polling and wakes when its bit is set (HoldActorUntilReleased sets it).

Out: RegisterSwitchOwner (switch_owner_table[n] = actor); the bit set (lib_bit_array.code_0273A2, Y = $1ADE, carry set = set): $16 bit $2000 cleared and jump; clear: CopExitSkip2 (the script then normally yields).
Clobbers: A, Y; the scratch of lib_bit_array; dp$38.
Cop1B_DelayThenGoto: Waits a number of frames, then continues at another address.
When: 211 scripts (timers, state machines, loops back to a poll such as COP 1B (&Poll, #$0004)).
Sees: a pause of delay + 1 frames.
Why: stores the resume address and the wait counter in one command.
In: &Code = target, Word = delay in frames.
Out: $18,X = target, $14,X = delay (the actor loop runs the script again when $14 goes below 0); yields.
Cop1F_StepRandom: When: 49 scripts, before a Cop35 draw.
Sees: nothing; the next draw differs.
Why: the state is a 16-byte additive generator ($0302-$0311) that only moves when a script asks.
In: no operand; X = actor (kept in Y meanwhile).
Out: bytes $0302-$0310 each receive the next byte added with a running carry (one CLC), then $0311 is incremented as a counter with the carry running up to $0302; continues; M = 16.
Clobbers: A (X restored from Y); dp none.
Cop27_YieldThenGoto: Yields now and continues at another address next frame.
When: 81 scripts, also the step command of the music-load actor (MusicLoadSendFade and the others).
Sees: a one-frame pause, then the target runs (a state machine step per frame).
Why: Cop1B with a delay of 0.
Cop31_FadeAndLoadMusic: Starts a music change with the full SPC handshake (fade command, stop command, upload).
When: 9 scripts: the front end (gv_front_end), village and cutscene actors with track $00, $12 and $13, and RunBossDeath with track $02 when the boss was not the last one.
Sees: the running music stops and the numbered track starts after a short silence; the game keeps running between the handshake steps, only the upload itself blocks.
Why: the sound CPU can only get a new song through the IPL upload, so a helper actor does the multi-frame handshake and ends itself.
In: Byte = track number (index into table_00FB49, 21 entries).

Out: a new actor before the caller (SpawnActorBefore) with $18/$36 = MusicLoadSendFade and $30 = track number; the caller continues. A full actor pool silently loses the request (Y = scratch slot $06AA).
Clobbers: A, Y = new slot; dp$38.
Cop32_StopAndLoadMusic: Starts a music change without the fade step (stop command, upload).
When: 5 scripts: tracks $00, $02, $0D and $11 (Grass Valley village, the trial room above, Death Toll's Shrine and the Magridd airship dock).
Sees: the music stops and the numbered track starts.
Why: same as Cop31, entering the chain at MusicLoadSendStop.
Out: new actor before the caller with $18/$36 = MusicLoadSendStop and $30 = track number.
Clobbers: A, Y = new slot; dp$38.
Cop35_RandomMod: Draws a random number below N.
Sees: random timing or direction of an actor.
Why: modulo by repeated subtraction of the byte $0302 of the generator.
Cop3B_JumpIfSwitchSetElseHold: Wakes a held NPC when its switch is set; otherwise keeps it waiting or sends it into the hold script.

When: 28 scripts, the first command of the villager and soul NPCs of the Mountain of Souls houses, Magridd's Castle, the Seabed Sanctuary, the Woods of Greenwood and Grass Valley, followed by COP 17 and the HoldActorUntilReleased tail.
Sees: a shut-in NPC either stays frozen until its lair switch is set, or acts normally (OQ-I025-1).
Why: two bits decide: the release switch of the lair record (word at +$1E of data_00BA0D, 0 = none) and the NPC's own switch n.
In: Word = lair record index n (also switch number), &Code = script of the active NPC.

Out: RegisterSwitchOwner(n). Release switch absent or set: switch n set: $16 bit $2000 cleared and jump; switch n clear: yield. Release switch not set: $34,X = n; bit $40 of lair_state[n] set: $16 bit $0010 set and CopExitSkip2 (continues into the hold code); bit clear: yield (OQ-I025-1).
Clobbers: A, Y; the scratch of lib_bit_array; dp$38.
Cop3C_SetTransitionType: Chooses the screen transition style of the next scene change.
When: 23 scripts, always just before a Cop10 (operand #$04 in all of them).
Sees: how the screen changes when the player leaves the scene.
Why: lib_scene_change_init reads transition_type; RunReturnLoop writes $80 for return trips.
Cop91_SetEntryHere: Makes the command after this one the re-entry point of the script.
When: 414 scripts (poll loops: COP 91, the checks, RTL).
Sees: nothing by itself; the actor repeats its checks every frame (wait for the player, a switch, a lair monster).
Why: after a yield the actor continues at $18,X; this command sets $18,X and $36,X to the next instruction, so a body ending in RTL re-runs from here.
Out: $36,X = script bank ($3A), $18,X = address after the command; continues (CopExitJump).

blockNote: COP commands for text, menus, items, Gems, EXP and HP. Commands (id, uses): 01 ShowText (608), 02 PromptYesNo (0), 0A GiveItemIfNotOwned (47), 0B RemoveItem (27), 18 JumpIfItemMissing (55), 19 JumpUnlessItemEquipped (36), 1A ChoiceMenu (27), 25 AddGems (0), 26 PayGemsOrJump (8), 36 AddExp (0), 37 HealPlayerToFull (12), 38 QueueExp (13), 39 DamagePlayer (6), 3A EnterPlayerName (1). Conventions shared by all handlers: cop_core block note.
=== INVENTORY ===

The inventory is the byte array inventory ($1B1E); entry n (1-based, the item id) is at $1B1E + n - 1: bits 0-6 hold the value (the entry number itself when owned; the engine's give routine lib_0109D6_part3.code_0120F9 writes it), bit 7 is the 'equipped' flag (OQ-I006-2). cop_core.LookupInventoryEntry reads an entry for Cop0A, Cop0B, Cop18 and Cop19. Ids seen in the scripts: $38 Medical Herb, $39 Strange Bottle, $40 Magic Bell (CheckPlayerDeath, engine_003005), $20-$29 (Cop19 in scene actors; names in plans/doc-audit/walkthrough-crosswalk.md section 4).
=== GEMS, EXP, HP ===

All three counters are BCD. Gems: gems_low ($1B66) and gems_high ($1B68), capped at 999999 by lib_player_stats.code_0276A5; the price check is code_0276C9 (carry set = not enough). EXP: player_exp ($1B78 low word, $1B7A high word). Cop38 does not add EXP directly: it stores the amount in exp_pending ($043D) and the main loop's code_027614 pays it out one digit step per 8 frames with sound. Cop37 sets heal_pending ($043B) = max HP - HP and code_0275ED heals one point every 4 frames. hud_dirty_flags ($0332) bit $04 redraws the HP bar, bit $02 the EXP and bit $10 the Gem counter.
=== TEXT AND MENUS ===

Cop01 passes a 16-bit string pointer in the script bank to lib_text_render.code_012C27 (DBR = script bank). Cop1A prints the option text (code_012769), runs lib_012281.code_012281 (A = number of entries; returns the chosen index in A, carry set = cancelled; sound $18 on choosing, $07 on cancelling), redraws (code_012BDA) and stores the index in choice_result ($03D0). The option strings are in shared_choice_prompt_texts (014F02 ' Yes / No' with 2 entries, 014F15 a single 'Yes', 014F23 'Record / Move / Quit' with 3 entries). Cop3A opens the name-entry screen (lib_name_entry.code_0124EE, name buffer from $1B92), used once at the start of the game after the Master's speech (the walkthrough: 'you will then get to pick a name for yourself').

Cop01_ShowText: Shows a text box with a string.
When: 608 scripts (every NPC line, sign and chest message).
Sees: the text window with the string.
Why: all text goes through one routine; the string is a 16-bit pointer in the script's own bank.
In: &ASCIIString = word pointer in the script bank.
Out: calls lib_text_render.code_012C27 with Y = pointer and DBR = script bank ($3A), then restores DBR and X and continues. The box handling is in the called routine (not annotated yet).
Cop02_PromptYesNo: Yes/No prompt with the fixed string asciistring_014F02; jumps unless Yes is chosen.
When: no script uses it (0 uses; OQ-I025-4); the same prompt is made by Cop1A with the same string.
Sees: ' Yes / No' with a cursor.
Why: probably the first version of Cop1A (inferred).
Out: runs the 2-entry menu (lib_012281.code_012281, A = 2); cancelled or choice not 0: jump; Yes: CopExitSkip2.
Cop0A_GiveItemIfNotOwned: Gives an item or progress entry unless the player already has it.
When: 47 scripts (chests, NPC gifts, shops): entry $38 (Medical Herb) in 7 of them, $39 (Strange Bottle) in 2.
Sees: the item is in the inventory afterwards; the pickup message is a separate Cop01.
Why: an owned entry stores its own number as value, so giving means writing the number into an empty entry.
Out: LookupInventoryEntry; value bits zero: lib_0109D6_part3.code_0120F9 stores the entry (not annotated yet); already owned: nothing. Continues.
Cop0B_RemoveItem: Removes an item (clears the value bits of its entry).
When: 27 scripts (CheckPlayerDeath removes the used Medical Herb or Strange Bottle; the others are in scene scripts).
Sees: the item disappears from the inventory.
Out: value bits 0-6 = 0; when bit 7 (equipped) was set the entry keeps $80 and equipped_bracelet ($1B64) is cleared; an empty entry is left alone. Continues.
Cop18_JumpIfItemMissing: Jumps when the player does not own an item.
Sees: NPCs and doors answer differently when the player lacks the item.
Out: value bits 0-6 zero: jump; owned: CopExitSkip2.
Cop19_JumpUnlessItemEquipped: Jumps unless the item is owned and its bit 7 is set.
When: 36 scripts: CheckPlayerDeath (Medical Herb $38, Strange Bottle $39, Magic Bell $40) and scene actors testing the ids $20-$29.
Sees: the death check consumes or ignores the item; actors react to a worn item.
Why: bit 7 is the equipped flag (OQ-I006-2).
Out: missing or bit 7 clear: jump; owned and bit 7 set: CopExitSkip2.
Cop1A_ChoiceMenu: Shows a text with a choice menu and jumps when the player cancels.
When: 27 scripts: Yes/No questions (asciistring_014F02, 014F43, 014F5B), a single 'Yes' (014F15) and 'Record / Move / Quit' (014F23).
Sees: the question with a cursor list; the player picks and confirms, or cancels.
Why: one menu command for every prompt; the choice is read later from choice_result.
In: &ASCIIString = option text, Byte = number of entries, &Code = target when cancelled.

Out: prints the string (lib_text_render.code_012769), runs lib_012281.code_012281 (A = entries; returns A = chosen index, carry set = cancelled), redraws (code_012BDA), vram_upload_flags = 1. Chosen: choice_result ($03D0) = index, CopExitSkip2; cancelled: jump.
Cop25_AddGems: When: no script uses it (0 uses; OQ-I025-4); Gem pickups use lib_player_stats.code_0276A5 directly.
Sees: the Gem counter would rise.
In: Word = amount in BCD (copdef lists two Bytes).
Out: lib_player_stats.code_0276A5 (BCD add, capped at 999999); hud_dirty_flags bit $10; continues.
Cop26_PayGemsOrJump: Charges the Gem cost of a spell, or jumps when the player cannot pay.
When: 8 uses: PayPhoenixCost (cost 2) and the spell scripts of player_spells_level_up (costs 1, 4, 8 and $20).
Sees: casting makes the Gem counter drop; with too few Gems the spell does not fire. The walkthrough: the Magic Bell prevents magic from using Gems, Magic Armor halves the consumption.
Why: every spell goes through one price check, and the two items change the price here.
In: Word = cost in BCD, &Code = target when the player is too poor.

Out: Magic Bell ($1B64 = $40): cost 0; Magic Armor ($1B60 = $0C): cost halved, at least 1; then lib_player_stats.code_0276C9 (BCD subtract; carry set = not enough, nothing taken). Paid: hud_dirty_flags bit $10 and CopExitSkip2; short: jump.
Cop36_AddExp: Adds to the EXP counter without a cap.
When: no script uses it (0 uses; OQ-I025-4); EXP is awarded by Cop38.
Why: unknown; unlike lib_player_stats.code_027687 it does not cap the sum at 99999999.
Out: player_exp ($1B78) + word in decimal mode, the carry into $1B7A.
Clobbers: A, Y; D flag restored; dp$38.
Cop37_HealPlayerToFull: Refills the player's HP over time.
When: 12 scripts (healing scenes in the Mountain of Souls, Leo's Laboratory, Greenwood, the Seabed Sanctuary and Magridd's Castle, and a shared helper).
Sees: the HP bar fills one point every 4 frames with a sound.
Why: the command only queues the amount; lib_player_stats.code_0275ED does the stepping.
Cop38_QueueExp: When: 13 scripts, amounts $0001, $0150, $0180, $0200, $0250, $0300 and $0400 (Lostside Marsh, Seabed of St. Elles, Leo's Laboratory, Mountain of Souls).
Sees: the EXP counter climbs in steps with a sound (one digit step per 8 frames, lib_player_stats.code_027614).
Why: rewards other than monster kills (the amount is queued, not added at once).
Out: exp_pending ($043D) = word (replaces an amount still waiting).
Cop39_DamagePlayer: Hurts the player by a fixed amount.
When: 6 scripts (hazards: World of Evil, Leo's Laboratory dungeon, the St. Elles coast, Lostside Marsh, Seabed of St. Elles).
Sees: HP drops and the player flinches.
Why: environmental damage that does not go through the contact-damage code.

Out: low byte of player_hp minus the damage (floor 0); hud_dirty_flags bit $04; the player actor's $26 = $FFE0; BRK #$04 (sound request); the player actor's $16 |= $0800 (hit stun). Death is detected by CheckPlayerDeath next frame.

Cop3A_EnterPlayerName: When: once, in gv_up_above_actors_and_name_entry (code_00798B), between 'you should have a name' and 'What an interesting name'.
Sees: the player chooses a name for himself (the walkthrough, In the Beginning: 'you will then get to pick a name for yourself').
Why: the name is typed into the buffer at $1B92 and printed later by the text codes.
Out: lib_name_entry.code_0124EE runs the screen; continues.

blockNote: COP commands that jump on a condition about actors, the player and the screen. Commands (id, uses): 0C JumpIfActorInBox (94), 0D JumpIfActorAtTile (76), 1C JumpIfActorFlags (6), 20 JumpIfPlayerOffGrid (3), 2E JumpIfActorInBoxWord (3), 89 / 8A JumpIfPlayerWithinX / Y (0 / 0), 8B / 8C JumpIfPlayerBeyondX / Y (0 / 0), 8D JumpIfOnScreen (0), 8E JumpIfOffScreen (0), 9A / 9B JumpByPlayerDeltaX / Y (175 / 174), 9C JumpByPlayerAxis (28), AD WaitUntilOnScreen (80). The other conditional jumps are in cop_script_flow_flags (flags, switches), cop_items_stats_text (items, Gems), cop_actor_fields_animation (Cop9E, CopA5) and cop_tiles_spawn_kill (tiles, Cop30).
=== CONVENTIONS ===

A jump command reads the &Code word at the script pointer and leaves through CopExitJump; a failed test leaves through the CopExitSkipN that matches the unread operand bytes (the position and slot operands are consumed first). Actor positions are x (left) and y (bottom edge) in pixels at $00/$02 of the actor; a box is the actor's width $10 and height $12. A tile operand is multiplied by 16 (TileToPixel); because y is the bottom edge, an actor standing on tile row n has y = (n + 1) x 16. Other actors are named by slot number 0-63 (SlotNumberToActor: $0800 + number x $40). player_x and player_y ($0374/$0376) are the player's position.
=== BOX TESTS ===

Cop0C and Cop2E (CopActorBoxTest) test whether the other actor's position lies inside the caller's box widened by a margin m: x in [x - m, x + m + width - 16] and y in [y - m - height + 16, y + m]. Cop0C takes m in tiles, Cop2E in pixels. Lair proximity scripts (RunLairProximity) use Cop0C; Cop0D tests for exactly one tile.
=== THREE-WAY BRANCHES ===

Cop9A and Cop9B take a threshold T and three targets: player left of (above) the actor by more than T, within the band, right of (below) it by T or more. Cop9C compares the X and Y distances to the player. They steer NPCs and enemies toward or away from the player; the usual follow-up is a facing or animation command.
=== UNUSED AND SUSPICIOUS ===

Cop89-Cop8E have no uses (OQ-I025-4). On the not-taken path Cop8D and Cop8E leave through CopExitContinue without skipping the &Code operand, so the script would run the target word as code (OQ-I001-1); harmless while unused. CopAD stops waiting once the actor is on screen or outside the map (it compares the actor position with map_width_px / map_height_px).

Cop0C_JumpIfActorInBox: Jumps when another actor's position is inside this actor's box widened by a margin in tiles.

=== FIELDS TOUCHED ===

Actor fields (engine_scheduler_sprites_combat_collision block note): $00/$02 x/y, $16 flags, $18 resume address, $1A attribute flags, $1C OAM attribute (bit 15 flip Y, bit 14 flip X, bits 12-13 priority, bits 9-11 palette), $1E animation id, $20 animation step, $22/$24 animation table and bank, $2A repeat counter, $2C/$34 dynamic-tile bank and source, $30 free parameter word. $1A: $8000 dynamic-tile sprite, $4000 draw in front, $2000 draw behind, $0080 not drawn.
=== ANIMATION COMMANDS ===

Cop80 and its relatives store the animation id in $1E, clear the step $20 and save the address after the command as the resume pointer. Cop82 then calls SetActorAnimFrame once per run: carry clear = a step was loaded, the actor yields and re-runs Cop82 next frame (the resume pointer points at it); carry set = the animation ended, the script goes on. Cop83 repeats the animation $2A times (set by Cop81). Cop92/Cop93/Cop94/Cop95 drive the stepper in lib_animation directly (code_01065B = advance, carry set = finished, code_0106CD = draw). Cop9D and Cop9E add the tile-blocked bit: $16 bit 2 is set when the actor ran into a solid tile.
=== SPRITE ATTRIBUTES ===

CopA2 and CopAA do not translate the operand: the byte is the high byte of the attribute, with the bits already in place (priority $10-$30, palette $02-$0E). CopA3/A4/A6/A7 set and clear the draw-order bits that CullAndSortActors turns into sort keys 0 (in front) and $01FE (behind). CopA8 sets the animation table pointer $22 and bank $24 (the effects bank $0E with table $8000 is used by RunAppearPuff); CopA9 turns an actor into a dynamic-tile sprite ($1A bit $8000).

The player is three actors: the player (player_actor $039C), the sword (player_weapon_actor $039E) and the soul orb (soul_orb_actor $03A0). Cop33 / Cop34 clear / set the not-drawn bit on all three and zero / increment player_hidden_count ($0464); while it is non-zero player_core clears joy_pressed. Cop2F moves the player actor and the actor linked at its $3E by a signed amount (used in ms_snow_mountain_actors and gw_lostside_marsh_actors for forced movement of 2 pixels per frame).

blockNote: COP commands for the tile map, spawning and killing actors. Commands (id, uses): 15 BlockOwnTiles (209), 16 UnblockOwnTiles (82), 21 JumpIfTileAbove (43), 22 JumpIfTileBelow (45), 23 JumpIfTileLeft (50), 24 JumpIfTileRight (47), 28 JumpIfTileHere (24), 29 JumpIfTileIdDiffers (0), 2A BlockTileAt (20), 2B UnblockTileAt (20), AE JumpIfTileTypeNonZero (52), 30 SpawnIfEnteredViaRecord (32), 84 SpawnActorAfter (13), 85 SpawnActorBefore (346), 86 KillSelf (283), AB SpawnAfterAbsolute (0), AC SpawnBeforeAbsolute (38), AF SpawnAfterWithFlags (12), B0 SpawnBeforeWithFlags (76), B1 SpawnAfterRelative (0). CopB2_SpawnBeforeRelative (114) is in cop_core. Conventions shared by all handlers: cop_core block note.
=== TILE MAP ===

tile_type_map ($7F8000) has one byte per 16x16 tile. The low nibble is the tile type (collision), the whole byte is non-zero for a solid tile; blocking an actor's tiles ORs $F0 into the byte (cop_core.BlockActorFootprint) and unblocking zeroes the byte (ClearActorFootprint, Cop2B). lib_map_index_helpers.code_0272B8 turns the pixel position in dp$16 (x) and dp$18 (y) into the byte index. y is the bottom edge of an actor, so the row the actor stands on is y - 16: Cop28 samples (x, y - 16), Cop21 (x, y - 16 - height) above the box, Cop22 (x, y) below it, Cop23 (x - 16, y - 16) left of it and Cop24 (x + width, y - 16) right of it. Cop21-Cop24 and Cop28 jump when the whole byte is non-zero (a block mark or a type); CopAE tests only the type nibble and takes its position relative to the actor. Cop2A/Cop2B use the same relative offsets. Cop29 (unused) compares the byte at $7E8000 + index with an operand.
=== SPAWNING ===

Operands: 84 / 85: @Code (word + bank byte); AF / B0: @Code, Word flags ($16); AB / AC: @Code, Word x, Word y, Word flags; B1 / B2: @Code, Word dx, Word dy, Word flags (position = the caller's plus the offset); 30: Word record index, @Code. Every variant allocates with SpawnActorAfter / SpawnActorBefore, which clone the caller (InitSpawnedActor), then store the entry in $18 and the bank in $36 and, depending on the variant, overwrite position and $16. With an empty free-slot stack the new actor lands in the scratch slot $06AA and nothing is linked (the handlers do not check the carry). Cop30 spawns only for a visit that began at lair record N: return_active ($03FB) non-zero and return_record ($0405, stored by the return-trip warp in lib_tile_triggers_and_lair_return) equal to the operand.
=== KILL ===

Cop86 unlinks the caller from the actor list ($3C next, $3E previous; heads $06A8 / $06A6) and pushes its slot on the free-slot stack. The script keeps running after the COP, which is why every kill is followed by RTL.

blockNote: CopB2_SpawnBeforeRelative, the exit chain and the helpers shared by every COP handler (file offsets 25715-26309, SNES $00:E473-$E6C5, bank 00). The handlers are in the cop_handlers files: cop_script_flow_flags, cop_items_stats_text, cop_conditions, cop_actor_fields_animation and cop_tiles_spawn_kill; the dispatcher and tables are in cop_dispatch.
=== CONVENTIONS OF EVERY HANDLER ===

HandleCop enters a handler with X = Y = the actor slot, DP $38 = the script pointer just past the id byte (the first operand byte) and DP $3A = the script bank. Every handler starts with TYX, reads its operands with LDA [$38] / INC $38 (a word costs two INCs; a Byte operand is read as a word and masked with $00FF) and leaves through the exit chain with BRL. A and Y are scratch; X is the actor slot again on exit, so the next COP of the script finds it intact. Scratch DP used by handlers: $00, $0C, $0E, $16, $18 (listed in each part note). A script that calls COP from its own code must keep X = actor slot (AGENTS.md, COP register requirement).

A jump command reads the target word and leaves through CopExitJump; a failed condition leaves through the CopExitSkipN that matches the operand bytes still unread. A wait command (Cop05, Cop82, Cop83, CopAD) does not move past itself while the wait lasts: it saves a resume pointer that re-runs the same COP next frame and yields. A command that spawns, kills or changes fields simply continues through CopExitContinue.
=== EXIT CHAIN ===

The chain (CopExitSkip5 .. CopExitYield) is entered by BRL from the handlers: CopExitSkip5 skips 5 operand bytes, CopExitSkip4 skips 4, CopExitSkip3 skips 3, CopExitSkip2 skips 2, CopExitSkip1 skips 1, CopExitContinue skips none. They fall through to CopExitJump, which writes A over the return address on the stack ($02,S) and returns with RTI, so the script continues at A (for a jump, A is the target). CopExitSaveResume stores $38 as the actor's resume pointer ($18,X) and falls into CopExitYield, which pops the COP frame and returns with RTL (yield to the actor loop).
=== FLAGS AND INVENTORY ===

Event flags are a bit array at $1A5E. A flag word has the bit number (0-7) in its low byte and the byte index in bits 8-14; bit 15 is a command-specific sense bit (Cop05_WaitWhileFlagEquals, Cop09_SetOrClearFlag). The inventory/progress bytes are at $1B1E (entry n at $1B1E + n - 1, bit 7 = flag, bits 0-6 = value).
=== ACTORS, TILES, SPAWNING ===

Actor slots are 0x40 bytes wide from $0800. Actors are in a doubly linked list ($3C = next, $3E = previous; heads $06A6 and $06A8). Free slots are kept on a stack addressed by $4A (word entries; a taken entry is zeroed); when it is empty PopFreeSlot returns the scratch slot $06AA with carry set and the spawn handlers, which never test the carry, write into that slot. The spawn helpers link a new actor after (SpawnActorAfter) or before (SpawnActorBefore) the caller and clone the caller's first $3C bytes into it (InitSpawnedActor); the handlers then set the entry address ($18, bank $36) and optionally position and $16. BlockActorFootprint and ClearActorFootprint write the $F0 block mark into tile_type_map ($7F8000) for the box of an actor (width $10, height $12; a box with width + height below $21 is one tile at (x, y - 16)).

Music load. Cop31 (FadeAndLoadMusic) and Cop32 (StopAndLoadMusic) spawn an actor whose script is the chain below; $30 of that actor is the track number, an index into table_00FB49 of data_00F9F7 (21 long pointers, 3 bytes each). Every step ends with COP 27 or COP 1B, so the steps are one or more frames apart and the game keeps running between them. APUIO0 ($2140) is the CPU-to-SPC port; the command meanings come from docs/audio/spc-disassembly.md (DispatchCommand).

MusicLoadSendFade: writes $F1 (the SPC's HandleFadeIn handler in that document) and waits (MusicLoadWaitFadeAck) until APUIO0 reads $F1 back, answers with $01 and waits (MusicLoadWaitSilence) until the port reads 0.
MusicLoadSendStop (Cop32 starts here): writes $F0 (StopAllChannels) and waits (MusicLoadWaitStopped) until the port reads 0, then COP 1B waits 2 frames.

MusicLoadUpload: writes $FF (the SPC's boot handshake handler), copies table_00FB49[$30] to dp$29-$2B and $0422/$0424, waits for vblank, switches NMI off (lib_system_helpers.code_0131AE), runs engine_spc_ipl_upload.code_0FEFF5 (the song data goes through the IPL transfer), waits for vblank and switches NMI on again (code_0131A2); COP 1B waits 2 frames.

MusicLoadFinish: writes $01, clears boss_fight_active ($0458, incremented by the boss scripts when the fight starts and read by the switch-tile code in lib_tile_triggers_and_lair_return) and kills the actor (COP 86). The meaning of the $F1 / $01 / 0 sequence is inferred from the wait loops (OQ-I025-2); the track numbers used are listed in cop_script_flow_flags (OQ-I025-3).

Respawn. RespawnOrKillActor is the tail of FinishEnemyDeath for enemies without a lair: with $1A bit $1000 clear the actor is killed (COP 86); with it set the actor stays dead until it has been off screen ($16 bit $8000) for $0258 + 1 frames ($26 counts down; on screen the count waits), then InitActorFromPlacement re-creates it in the same slot from its placement record ($3A).

MusicLoadSendFade: Step 1 of a music change started by Cop31: sends command $F1 to the SPC.
When: first script of the actor spawned by Cop31_FadeAndLoadMusic.
Sees: the running music is told to fade (the SPC handler is HandleFadeIn in docs/audio/spc-disassembly.md; the direction of the fade is not verified, OQ-I025-2).
Why: the SPC must be quiet before a new song can be uploaded through the IPL.
In: X = the spawned actor, $30 = track number.
Out: APUIO0 = $F1; COP 27 continues at MusicLoadWaitFadeAck next frame.
MusicLoadWaitFadeAck: Waits for the SPC to echo $F1, then answers $01.
When: every frame after MusicLoadSendFade until the echo arrives (RTL re-runs it).
Why: handshake: the command is only taken as delivered when the SPC returns it.
Out: APUIO0 = $F1: APUIO0 = $01 and COP 27 continues at MusicLoadWaitSilence; otherwise RTL.
MusicLoadWaitSilence: Waits until APUIO0 reads 0, then goes on to MusicLoadSendStop.
When: every frame after the answer $01.
Sees: nothing; the old music is already fading or silent.
Why: the port returns to 0 when the SPC has finished the fade (inferred, OQ-I025-2).
Out: APUIO0 = 0: branches to MusicLoadSendStop; otherwise RTL.
MusicLoadSendStop: Sends command $F0 (stop all channels) to the SPC.
When: after the fade handshake, or as the first script of the actor spawned by Cop32_StopAndLoadMusic.
Why: the upload may only start on a stopped SPC.
Out: APUIO0 = $F0; COP 27 continues at MusicLoadWaitStopped next frame.
MusicLoadWaitStopped: Waits until APUIO0 reads 0, then waits 2 frames before the upload.
Why: the SPC clears the port when the stop command is done.
Out: APUIO0 = 0: COP 1B continues at MusicLoadUpload after 2 frames; otherwise RTL.
MusicLoadUpload: Uploads the track to the SPC.
When: 2 frames after the SPC reported stopped.
Sees: the new music starts shortly after; the upload itself runs with NMI off, so the game stalls for a moment.
Why: this is the only way to change songs: the SPC program and the song data are transferred through the IPL protocol (engine_spc_ipl_upload).

Out: APUIO0 = $FF; $30 = 0; the long pointer table_00FB49[track] is in dp$29-$2B and $0422/$0424; vblank wait, NMI off, code_0FEFF5 upload, vblank wait, NMI on; COP 1B continues at MusicLoadFinish after 2 frames.
Clobbers: A, Y; DP $29-$2B; X preserved (PHX/PLX).
MusicLoadFinish: Releases the SPC and ends the music-load actor.
Why: the $01 byte lets the SPC leave its handshake; boss_fight_active is cleared because the boss track change marks the end of the boss fight.
Out: APUIO0 = $01, boss_fight_active ($0458) = 0, COP 86 kills the actor.
RespawnOrKillActor: Last step of an enemy's death without a lair: kills it, or lets it come back later.
Sees: the enemy is gone; a respawning enemy returns as a fresh copy after the player has left it off screen for about 10 seconds.
Why: ordinary field enemies come back, scripted ones (and bosses) do not; $1A bit $1000 decides.
In: X = dying actor, $3A = its placement record.

Out: $1A bit $1000 clear: COP 86. Set: $26 = $0258, COP 91; each frame while $16 bit $8000 (off screen) is set $26 is decremented and when it goes negative InitActorFromPlacement re-creates the actor in this slot; on screen nothing counts.
